title: A Savings Thermometer Poster
description: Turn a savings goal into a picture you can see every day: a big thermometer on the wall that fills up, one coloured-in step at a time, until the goal is reached.

body.heading: How it works
paragraphs: Pick one goal and one number: say, $200 for a new bike, or $500 for a holiday fund. Draw a tall thermometer shape on a large sheet of paper, mark it in ten equal steps, and write the amount next to each step. Stick it somewhere the household will see it every day — the fridge, or the hallway wall.

Every time money goes into the savings, colour in the matching part of the thermometer. A $20 deposit on a $200 goal fills two steps. Watching the red climb is the whole point: a goal you can see is a goal you keep feeding, and children who colour in the steps learn that saving is something you do, not just something adults talk about.

body.heading: Keep it honest and visible
paragraphs: Colour in only what has truly been saved, even when progress is slow. A half-filled thermometer that tells the truth is more motivating than a finished one that does not. If progress stalls for a while, add a small step — a coin jar, a no-spend day — rather than lowering the goal.

When the thermometer is full, celebrate the moment before you spend it: take a photo, mark the date, and then start a fresh poster for the next goal. The habit of seeing savings grow is worth more than any single target.

takeaway: A goal you can see is a goal you keep feeding.
materials: A large sheet of paper or card
A marker pen and a ruler
Sticky tape or magnets to hang the poster
supervision: A household member agrees the goal amount and the target date together before the poster goes up, and checks the coloured-in total against the real savings each week.
safetyNotes: Keep the poster where only your household sees it if the amounts feel private
Colour in only what you have truly saved, so the picture stays honest
Use child-safe scissors if a younger helper cuts out decorations
